patients.summary: Senior financial analyst who joins the practice at 48 with unexplained chronic liver disease, severe hypercholesterolemia after atorvastatin myopathy, and joint pain. Diabetes appears in 2025, cardiology names familial hypercholesterolemia and adds colesevelam, and in 2026 gastroenterology finds hereditary hemochromatosis with arthropathy and starts phlebotomy.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is looking to join the practice. Moving his care from a practice he has used for years, says he wants a doctor he can actually reach. Works long hours in finance, prefers early morning slots. Insurance BCBS PPO, card info taken. Booked new pt visit 9/12 at 7:40 am. Asked him to bring his med bottles and sign a records release at check-in so we can request his old chart. He said his old office has his labs "for the liver thing and the cholesterol."

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

48 yo man transferring care. Says his prior office was fine but he could never get a call back. Wants one place that keeps track of his liver numbers and his cholesterol.

HPI / history as he tells it:
- Liver: told several years ago his liver enzymes were "high and staying high." Never drinks, never has. He recalls blood tests and being told nothing specific was found; no records with him. No jaundice, no swelling of the belly or legs that he has noticed.
- Cholesterol: has known it is very high for a long time. Was put on atorvastatin around 2021 and within weeks had aching in his thighs, shoulders and arms; blood test showed a muscle enzyme elevation and the drug was stopped. Started on ezetimibe after that and has taken it daily since. Not on anything else for lipids.
- Joints: aching and stiffness in several joints that his old office called inflammatory arthritis. Takes acetaminophen 500 mg when it flares, a few times a week. Never seen rheumatology.
- Gallbladder out in 2018, uncomplicated.

Meds: ezetimibe 10 mg daily; acetaminophen 500 mg q6h prn joint pain; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: atorvastatin (myalgias with CK rise) -- intolerance; sulfa antibiotics -- rash.
Family: father had an MI at 42 and high cholesterol. Mother has type 2 diabetes. One brother has cirrhosis, cause never explained to the family as far as he knows.
Social: senior financial analyst, long weeks especially in close periods. Single, lives alone. Never smoked, no alcohol ever, no drugs. Walks most evenings.

ROS: no chest pain, no exertional symptoms, no GI bleeding, no change in bowels. Otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic scars, no organomegaly appreciated. No edema. Joints without effusion or warmth today, full range in hands, wrists, knees. Skin no rash. Neuro grossly normal. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Chronic liver disease, cause not established -- CMP today, will get the old workup.
2. Severe hypercholesterolemia on ezetimibe, statin intolerant -- lipid panel today. Strong family history. Likely needs a lipid specialist; will decide once I see numbers.
3. Inflammatory arthropathy per prior list -- acetaminophen as needed, quiet today.
4. Health maintenance: HCV and HIV screen today (he agrees), A1c. Will ask the prior office about colonoscopy and vaccines.

Records release signed. RTC about 6 months, sooner as needed.

orders.reason: Severe hypercholesterolemia on ezetimibe, statin intolerant, father MI at 42

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Viktor,

Your results are back. Kidney function, blood counts and sugar (A1c 5.5) are normal. The hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative.

Your liver enzymes are up: AST 66 and ALT 79. That matches what you told me, and I will compare against your old records when they arrive.

Your LDL is 192 on ezetimibe, which is high, and with your father's heart attack at 42 I think it is worth having a cardiologist who focuses on cholesterol weigh in. I have put in the referral. Their office should call you; if you don't hear in two weeks, let us know.

Best,
Your PCP

documents.title: Prior primary care records summary
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received by fax, 6 pages: problem list, medication list, immunization record, one procedure report. No lab reports included.

PROBLEM LIST (prior office): elevated liver enzymes / chronic liver disease, etiology undetermined; hypercholesterolemia, severe; statin myopathy (atorvastatin) 2021; joint pain - inflammatory arthropathy; s/p cholecystectomy 2018.

MEDICATIONS: ezetimibe 10 mg daily (started 2021 after atorvastatin discontinued for myalgias and CK elevation); acetaminophen 500 mg PRN; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily.

ALLERGIES: atorvastatin - myalgia/CK elevation; sulfa - rash.

IMMUNIZATIONS: Tdap 06/2019.

PROCEDURE: screening colonoscopy 11/2021 to the cecum, good prep, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.

Scanned to chart. -- MA

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work for vaccines. No fever today, no prior vaccine reactions. Flu quadrivalent 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Pfizer 2023-24 formula 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction. Asked about the cardiology referral -- he has the number, hasn't called yet, "quarter end."

documents.title: Ezetimibe refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax requesting new rx for ezetimibe 10 mg -- prior prescriber's refills exhausted. Last fill 12/2023. Routed to PCP. Approved 90 days x 3 refills, e-sent.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month follow-up. Feels fine. Joints about the same, uses acetaminophen a couple of times a week, never more than 2 tablets a day. Taking ezetimibe daily. Has not scheduled with cardiology -- work has been heavy, says he will get to it. Old records came: they confirm the atorvastatin story, colonoscopy 2021 clean, but no lab reports and nothing about how the liver was worked up.

O: Vitals per flowsheet. Alert, comfortable. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema.

A/P:
- Chronic liver disease, cause unclear: repeat hepatic panel today. With chronic liver disease he should be protected against hep A and B -- he agrees. Heplisav-B #1 and hep A #1 today.
- Hypercholesterolemia: lipids today. Encouraged him again to see cardiology.
- Joints: acetaminophen as needed.
RTC September for physical.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Viktor -- liver enzymes are about where they were in September, not climbing. LDL still about 190. Same plan: ezetimibe, and please make that cardiology appointment when you can. Nurse visit in about a month for the second hepatitis B shot.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Will book the nurse visit. Cardiology I will look at after tax season.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Heplisav-B dose 2 of 2, 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Tolerated dose 1 without problems. Series complete. Hep A dose 2 due in the fall -- reminder set for his flu shot visit.

documents.title: Referral follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Cardiology office notified us the referral expired, never scheduled (3 attempts to reach pt). Called pt: he would rather hold off for now and keep working on diet; will bring it up at his physical. Referral closed. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL -- 49M

Interval: no new problems. Joints unchanged, acetaminophen as needed. Ezetimibe daily, vitamin D daily. Still walking most evenings. Sleep ok when work allows.

We talked about cardiology again. He would like to give diet another year before adding appointments; he has cut back on red meat and cheese. I told him I think he is underestimating his risk with his father's history, and he heard that. Revisit at next physical, sooner if anything changes.

ROS negative for chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, GI symptoms, urinary symptoms.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. General well. Eyes, ears, oropharynx normal. Neck no nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft nontender, no masses or organomegaly. Extremities no edema. Joints without synovitis. Skin unremarkable. PHQ-2 0.

Prevention: colonoscopy 2021 normal. Tdap 2019. Heplisav-B complete; hep A #2 with flu shot next month. Hep C/HIV done 2023.

Plan: CMP, lipids, A1c today. Return in spring for liver follow-up.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Viktor, A1c 5.6, kidneys fine. Liver enzymes steady compared with last year. LDL 188 -- diet changes haven't moved it much, which is typical when the cause is mostly genetic. The cardiology door is open whenever you want it. Flu shot and hep A #2 next month.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu 0.5 mL IM L deltoid; Moderna 2024-25 0.5 mL IM R deltoid; Hep A adult dose 2 of 2, 1 mL IM L deltoid (separate site). Screening questions negative. Observed 15 min, fine. Hep A series complete.
